label: rem:kelvin-classical-limit
title: Classical limit of the $q$-Kelvin dispersion
html:
Remark. Classical limit of the q-Kelvin dispersion

As q \to 1, the components resolve to their classical definitions: [k]_q \to k, \Gamma_q \to j(j+1), and \nu_q \to 0. The q-Kelvin dispersion immediately recovers the classical form \omega_k = \Gamma k^2 / (4\pi a^2) \cdot (\ln(L/a) - c). The Biot--Savart self-induction integral generates the classical logarithmic factor; the q-deformation subsumes this logarithm directly into the deformed core radius a_q.
